name: Aaron Meacham

sections.Description:
Aaron Meacham teaches Health Communications and International Health at BYU-Idaho. His interest in public health came from learning about emergency response as a undergraduate at BYU-Idaho. He went on to complete a Master's in Public Health degree from BYU in Provo, Utah. in 2007. Afterwards, Aaron completed a doctorate at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City in 2014. He then worked for several years with Latter-day Saint Charities providing public health services before moving to Rexburg, Idaho, where he has been a part of BYU-Idaho's Department of Health Services since 2017.

One of the great benefits of public health, says Dr. Meacham, is that it is so diverse.

name: Aaron Miller

Education: DMA Double Bass Performance, Northwestern University
MM Jazz Performance and Pedagogy, University of Colorado Boulder
sections.Bio: Aaron Miller, Director of Jazz StudiesAaron Miller likes music. He likes old music, new music, folk music and dance music. Music has always played an important part in his life. As a young boy, playing the bass in jazz clubs, pit and community orchestras helped Aaron find meaning and security during his growing up years. He was drawn to the string bass because it was present in almost all types of music and allowed for a variety of performance opportunities. Aaron’s enjoyment of music led him to complete a Master’s in jazz performance and pedagogy from the University of Colorado and a Doctorate of Musical Arts in double bass performance from Northwestern University. Aaron’s performances have included touring with the Glenn Miller Orchestra, the second national tour of The Producers, and the South American premier of Macedonian composer Zivojin Glisic’s Concerto for Double Bass. Sometimes, Aaron teaches music. He enjoys working with collegiate bassists at BYU-Idaho, encouraging young musicians at the Red Lodge Music Festival, and instructing the next generation of jazz musicians in eastern Idaho. The relative cultural isolation and slower pace of Rexburg suits Aaron’s other interests of spending time with his family, pursuing endurance sports, riding his bicycle, avoiding social media in all its forms, and doing anything with his Great Dane Mingus. Mingus would prefer that the order of Aaron’s passions were feed Mingus more, play with Mingus more, allow Mingus to sit on his lap more, take Mingus camping more and feed Mingus...more. It’s Aaron’s hope that we will all pursue what we enjoy more and look for ways to support each other in those pursuits.

name: Adam Ballif

sections.Description:
Dr. Adam Ballif holds a Doctor of Musical Arts and a Master of Music degree in clarinet performance from Arizona State University. Dr. Ballif joined the faculty of Brigham Young University-Idaho in 2012. Previously he was Associate Professor of Music at Colorado Mesa University where he taught clarinet and saxophone, and coordinated the music education program. Before Colorado, Dr. Ballif was Assistant Professor of Clarinet at the University of Evansville in Evansville, Indiana and served as Principal Clarinetist with the Evansville Philharmonic Orchestra. He received his Bachelor's Degree in Music Education from Brigham Young University. While in Utah, he performed with the Orchestra at Temple Square, which included performing with the Mormon Tabernacle Choir and recording soundtracks for motion pictures. In July 2002, Dr. Ballif participated in the Belgium Clarinet Academy and presented a paper titled, "Benny Goodman Influences Classical Composition," at the 2002 International Clarinet Association's convention in Stockholm Sweden. In Arizona he was principal clarinetist with the Mesa Symphony Orchestra and taught instrumental music at the elementary and middle school levels. His principal clarinet teachers include Robert Spring, William Holman, and Alan Stanek. Dr. Ballif remains active as a performer and clinician.

For more clarinet resources, studio materials, and recordings please visit Dr. Ballif's personal website:

www.adamballif.com

Education: B.S. in Business Administration (emphasis on Marketing) from San Jose State University
MBA (focus on Technology and Innovationfrom) from San Jose State University
sections.Bio:
Alan Thompson is a professor of Business Management at Brigham Young University – Idaho. While earning his B.S. in Business Administration (emphasis on Marketing) from San Jose State University, he worked at Sun Microsystems, Inc. in various technical and engineering roles. He also earned his MBA from San Jose State University with a focus on Technology and Innovation. In 1997, Alan jumped into Digital Marketing and Advertising, where he worked until early 2016 in various Product Marketing positions and leading different organizations. Over the course of his career, Alan worked at multiple Internet and Digital Marketing companies including: Netscape, AdForce, Yahoo!, Experian, TransUnion, Ipsos and Epsilon. In his various positions, he has provided digital marketing solution to many top brands such as: Ford, Marriott, AT&T, GM, Landrover/Jaguar, P&G, American Express, and Disney. Alan also taught at Northwestern University as an adjunct professor for 9 years.

He has 2 totally awesome children ages 24 and 20, and has been married to his wonderful wife Juls for nearly 30 years. He currently resides in Rexburg, ID. As an interesting side note, Alan has performed the “dying” scene at Disney MGM Studios (Florida) in the Indiana Jones Adventure show 5 times!

Alan is also an author of a Supernatural Sci-Fi thriller trilogy titled “Creation Abomination”. He is really putting his digital marketing skills to the test since this is completely self-published.

name: Alicia McQuay
image_alt: Photo of Alicia McQuay with a harp.

sections.Description:
A native of Provo, Utah, Alicia Duncan McQuay made her professional orchestral debut to great critical acclaim at the age of 17 as harp soloist performing with the Utah Symphony under the direction of Keith Lockhart. Born into a musical family, Alicia began studying harp at the age of 4 and has since appeared in concert as soloist, chamber musician, and symphony harpist throughout the United States.

Alicia McQuay holds the degree Doctor of Music in Harp Performance and Literature from the world renowned Jacobs School of Music at Indiana University where she was a student of Susann McDonald. A dedicated and passionate teacher, she served as Professor McDonald's teaching assistant and also was a harp instructor on the faculty of the Pre-College Harp Program. Her students have been prize-winners in prestigious harp competitions and are frequently admitted to top harp performance programs across the country.

Alicia holds a Bachelor of Music degree from the Brigham Young University School of Music where she studied with ShruDeLi Ownbey and Louise Vickerman and a Master of Music degree from Indiana University.

In 2014 Alicia was appointed as principal harpist of the Idaho Fall Symphony and continues to enjoy an active performance career. Alicia is currently Professor of Music (Harp) at Brigham Young University-Idaho where she is the director of the harp performance program.

sections.Bio: Amy Clark earned a doctorate degree with a focus on reading, literacy, and assessment, a master’s degree in early childhood special education, and a bachelor's degree in elementary education. She taught young children in preschool, kindergarten, first, and third grades for seventeen years in Phoenix, Denver, and Idaho Falls before coming to BYU Idaho in 2015. Amy's educational focus is on literacy instruction. She loved teaching children to read and now enjoys sharing her love of reading with future teachers. Amy enjoys climbing mountains, rowing down rivers, and being in the outdoors with her family.

name: Amy De Vera
image_alt: A photo of Amy De Vera

sections.Biography:
Amy De Vera is a dancer, choreographer, and educator. She received her bachelor's in dance choreography and performance from BYU-Idaho, graduating with honors through the National Honors Society for Dance Arts. She received her YTT 200 certification through Yoga Alliance in 2018, is a member of the National Dance Education Organization, and is currently an adjunct faculty member at BYU-Idaho.

Amy loves teaching and helping her students grow, make connections, and discover themselves through movement. She strives to create a supportive learning environment where students are encouraged to question and think critically. She has taught a variety of subjects at the university, including Modern Technique, Jazz Technique, Conditioning for Dancers, Somatics, Choreography and Improvisation, Kinesiology, Yoga, Philosophies and Techniques of Teaching Dance, served as artistic director of “A BYU-Idaho Christmas”, and assistant director for Dance Alliance several times.

Amy has taught and choreographed for professional companies, musicals, and studios throughout Utah and Idaho for over 15 years. Her choreography has received accolades throughout the West, including being recognized in Salt’s SHAPE Festival in 2019. In Boise, Idaho, Amy helped establish CADA Dance Studio, which won an award for Best of Idaho in 2022.

As a performer, Amy danced with The Dance Collaborative and set original choreography for the company throughout two seasons. In 2019, she performed in Dichotomy, an evening-length work set by Ashley Storm and Joy Esplin Harris. She also performed for three seasons with BYU-Idaho’s Dance Alliance, touring across the US and Canada.

When she’s not teaching or creating, Amy enjoys baking bread, reading, spending time with family and friends, and doing yoga.

name: Amy DeMordaunt

sections.Description:
Amy DeMordaunt has a Master's in Nursing from the University of Arizona, where she specialized in Clinic Systems Leadership. She completed her undergraduate work at BYU-Idaho.

Professer DeMordaunt has extensive experience in the nursing field, having serves as a registered nurse at several medical centers in Utah, Arizona, Illinois, Colorado, Idaho, California, and Ohio. After serving for five years as a clinical educator at Madison Memorial Hospital in Rexburg, Idaho, she accepted a faculty position at BYU-Idaho.

Amy enjoys training a new generation of nurses and is noted for her caring, positivity, and outstanding experience.

name: Andrew Allphin

sections.Description:
Andrew Allphin is a trumpet performer and educator. Prior to joining the faculty at Brigham Young University-Idaho, he was a trumpeter in The United States Army Band “Pershing’s Own” in Washington D.C. since 2004. “Pershing’s Own is the premiere ensemble of the Army, and as a member of “Pershing’s Own” he performed regularly in ceremonies and concerts of national significance. He performed “Taps” hundreds of times yearly at The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, and for fallen heroes in Arlington National Cemetery. Sergeant First Class Allphin performed at the funerals of Presidents Ronald Reagan and Gerald R. Ford, and participated in the inaugurals of three U.S. presidents. Dr. Allphin played regularly in concerts as a member of t he U.S. Army Concert Band, the U.S. Army Herald Trumpets for dignitaries and heads of state, the U.S. Army Brass Quintet, the U.S. Army Blues, and the U.S. Army Band Trumpet Ensemble. As a founding member of the U.S. Army Band Trumpet Ensemble, he was a featured artist at the International Trumpet Guild Festival in Sydney, Australia, and the Sauerland-Herbst Music Festival in Germany. Andrew Allphin also fulfilled a diplomatic mission to China where he performed multiple concerts with the premiere musical organization in China, The People’s Liberation Army Band. As a member of “Pershing’s Own,” he also participated in several recording projects.

As a performing musician, he has entertained in world renowned venues such as the Kennedy Center, Strathmore, Wolf Trap, the Lincoln Center, and the National Center for the Performing Arts in Beijing, China. He has performed with greats such as Vince DiMartino, Jens Lindemann, Marvin Stamm, Conrad Herwig, Joseph Alessi, Carol Jantsch, Mnozil Brass, and Rhythm and Brass. Andrew has performed regularly with the National Symphony Orchestra and the Annapolis Symphony. He has performed with other orchestras such as the Plymouth Symphony, Maryland Symphony, Windsor Symphony, and the North Carolina Symphony.

Andrew holds the degree Doctor of Musical Arts from The Catholic University of America, Master of Music from the University of Michigan, and Bachelor of Music from Brigham Young University. He studied trumpet with William Campbell, David Brown, Steve Hendrickson, and Adel Sanchez. Dr. Allphin was previously an adjunct Professor of Trumpet and the Director of Brass Ensembles at The Catholic University of America in Washington D.C. He also taught at Strayer University as a Professor of Humanities, and was a faculty member at Bishop Ireton High School, a renowned school for music education.

name: Andrew Hyde

sections.Description:
Andrew Hyde graduated from BYU-Idaho in 2006 with a degree in Health Services, Allied, Health, and Health Sciences. He then completed a physical therapy program at Nova Southeastern University, earning a Doctor of Physical Therapy. He worked for over a decade as a director and physical therapist for Star Therapy Services before accepting a faculty position at BYU-Idaho in 2022.

Professor Hyde emphasizes that there is a spiritual application to everything, including health and human performance. He loves teaching students and helping others improve their quality of life.

sections.Bio:
Angelia Watkins has been teaching at BYU Idaho since 2012. Prior to that, she worked for the United States Congressional House Budget Office in Washington, DC and for Covey Leadership Center in Provo, Utah. She also served on the Board of Trustees, including serving as the Board Chair, of Eastern Idaho Regional Medical Center.

name: Ashley Reed

sections.Biography:
Ashley Reed is a dedicated ballroom dance educator with a rich background in competitive dance and teaching. Originally from Idaho Falls, ID, Ashley discovered her passion for dance at an early age, inspired by her siblings' involvement in the sport. Her journey began on her high school's ballroom team and flourished at the Idaho Ballroom Academy (IBA), where she represented the academy at the prestigious Blackpool Dance Festival in 2008.

During her time at Brigham Young University-Idaho (BYU-I), Ashley immersed herself in the vibrant dance community, assuming diverse roles as a competitor, performer, student teacher, director, and choreographer within esteemed organizations like the BYU-I Latin Team, Collegiate Dancers, and Dance Alliance. Her commitment extended beyond campus, coaching youth teams at IBA while also competing with their Adult Medley Teams.

Upon graduating, Ashley joined the BYU-I Dance Department as Adjunct Faculty, focusing on refining the technical proficiency of aspiring dancers. She finds fulfillment in nurturing their growth and fostering artistic expression through strong fundamentals. Concurrently, she continued coaching at IBA for six years, competing for three of those years. In this time, she married her high school sweetheart and former ballroom teammate. Together, they enjoy a variety of activities including traveling, concerts, sporting events, paddle boarding, and spending time with their dog.

Ashley remains dedicated to advancing her craft, having earned her Bronze American Smooth certification with DanceVision and actively pursuing further certifications and personal development. In 2023, she participated in an international European ballroom tour, supporting one of her couples as they trained for and competed at the German Open Championships. This experience not only intensified her love for dance but also exposed her to top-tier competition, igniting her pursuit of excellence.

sections.Bio: Ashley is a dancer, choreographer and educator. She is currently an Associate Professor at Brigham Young University Idaho and has taught at the University of Utah, Utah Valley University, Brigham Young University as well as several residencies at universities throughout the North West as a member of Repertory Dance Theater. She has performed with Repertory Dance Theater out of Salt Lake City, Performing Dance Company of the University of Utah, and Dancers Company of Brigham Young University. She has had the opportunity to perform works choreographed by Zvi Gotheiner, Robert Battle, Andrea Miller, Elizabeth Waters, Susan Hadley, Isadora Duncan, Ruth St. Dennis, Doris Humphrey, Helen Tamiris, Jose` Limon, Lar Lubovitch, Laura Dean, Bill Evens, Lisa Race, Andy Vacca, Carley Conders, Abby Fiat and Stephen Koester. Ashley has choreographed works for Repertory Dance Theater, the University of Utah, Utah Valley University, and Brigham Young University Idaho. She is one of the directors for Dance Alliance, Brigham Young University Idaho’s premiere touring dance company. Ashley is a certified Pilates instructor and has experience in Modern, Jazz and Ballet styles as well as Composition, Dance for Film, Improvisation, Barteniuff Fundamentals, Laban Movement Analysis and the Tanner method of Creative Dance for children. She has been awarded the Golden Apple teaching award from Brigham Young University Idaho, the Dee Winterton Excellence in teaching award from the University of Utah, and been named performer of the year at the University of Utah and Brigham Young University, as well as Student of the Year at Utah Valley University. At Brigham Young University Idaho she currently teaches Advanced Technique and Somatic Studies, Advanced Composition, Improvisation, Conditioning for Dancers, Introduction to Dance and Career, Advanced Jazz Dance and she mentors the student senior capstone projects and directs various dance companies on campus. She recently completed an evening-length piece entitled Dichotomy, which debuted in 2019. Ashley is currently serving as the Associate Chair of the Department of Theatre and Dance at Brigham Young University Idaho. She continues to build her local community through dance as she works with youth groups of all ages. She is a member of the National Dance Education Organization and serves on the executive board for the Idaho Dance Education Organization. Along with her passion for her work, some of her greatest joys in life come from being a wife and a mother to her three beautiful children.

name: Aubrie Mema
image_alt: A professional photo of Adjunct Faculty Aubrie Mema.

sections.Artist Statement:
The world is increasingly plagued by division, with rifts permeating various aspects of society. These divisions are manifested in politics, religion, and social issues, creating a complex landscape. I am interested in exploring these divisions as a dynamic interplay of oppositions. This exploration aims to delve into the friction and synergy that arise when differing perspectives collide or attempt to coexist.

In my work, I seek to portray the nuanced interplay between opposing forces. By examining how conflict and cooperation emerge from these divisions, I seek to highlight both the discord and potential harmony that can exist within society. Through my art, I desire to capture the essence of these interactions, showcasing how oppositional elements can both challenge and complement each other, ultimately contributing to a more profound understanding of the human experience.
sections.Biography: Aubrie MEMA was raised in Cincinnati, Ohio. She received her BFA from Utah State University and is presently enrolled in the MFA program at The School of the Art Institute of Chicago. She recently completed a residency at the Idaho Art Lab. Recent exhibitions include solo shows at The Tirana International Hotel, Albania; Rome Temple Visitor’s Center, Italy; Lushnjë City Cultural Hall, Albania; Fairfax Schlesinger Art Center, USA; and Touchstone Gallery, Washington, DC, USA. Recent group exhibitions include The LDS Church History Museum, Salt Lake City; National History Museum, Albania; Anne C. Fisher Gallery, Washington, DC. and Zenit Art Gallery, Tirana, Albania. AMEMA’s work is included in numerous personal collections. She is an Adjunct Professor at Brigham Young University Idaho and lives and works in Rexburg, Idaho.

name: Autumn Hawkes

sections.Biography:
Autumn, raised in Ammon Idaho, will often joke that she was born dancing. She began her dance career as a dedicated ballerina before trading in her pointe shoes for Latin heels in 2010. For the next 10 years, Autumn trained, competed, and performed as a ballroom dancer, first at Extreme Ballroom and later as a member of the BYU Ballroom Touring Company. In addition to being an accomplished Latin dancer both individually and on team, Autumn was also exceptional at cabaret, winning two national titles as a youth dancer and placing in the top three nationally numerous times as an adult.

As a dance major at Brigham Young University, Autumn refined her skills and passion for ballroom while also studying a myriad of other styles including ballet, contemporary, tap, world, and modern dance. In 2019, she traveled to Blackpool, England, to compete at the British Championships with the BYU team, where they secured first place in the Latin formation category. During her three years on the touring company, Autumn showcased her talent and love of dance through extensive travel across Europe and North America. While at BYU, Autumn taught university classes in social dance, country dance, and international Latin technique. She also spent a year as a coach in the Utah area elementary ballroom program. In 2020, she graduated with a Dance B.A., and the following year she taught ballet and tap at a fine arts preschool. Most recently, Autumn has taught Latin technique and coaches private Latin and cabaret couples while also coaching competitive medley teams at Extreme Ballroom.

With her broad dance background, Autumn brings a well-rounded approach to dance education. She has been teaching dance since 2016, and has worked with dancers of all ages and skill levels. She is passionate about nurturing individual growth, artistic self-expression, excellent technique, and a love of dance in her students. Autumn has experience doing choreography for both individual competitors and large show groups. She excels in crafting routines for dancers of all levels, from beginners to advanced performers.

Autumn finds the most joy in her family and cherishes special moments with her husband, son, and dog. An outdoor enthusiast, she enjoys long walks, bike rides, and drawing inspiration from nature. Autumn also loves sunny beach getaways, yoga classes, and a competitive game of Spikeball in the backyard. Known for her laughter and fun-loving nature, she enjoys engaging in conversations and spreading smiles wherever she goes.

sections.Biography: Bill was born in Logan, Utah where he lived until he finished the 8th grade. He then moved with his family to Erda, Utah (Tooele County) to live and work on his uncle's Jersey Dairy farm while attending Tooele High School. After high school, Bill served a mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints in British Columbia, Canada. He loved teaching the people there about the life, ministry, and teachings of Jesus Christ. After returning from Canada, he met Jessica Salas at Snow College in Ephraim, Utah. They loved their time at Snow College! It was at Snow college after his mission that his passion for teaching overcame his longstanding plan of being an aerospace engineer. Bill and Jessica were married and then continued their education at Weber State University. After they both graduated from Weber State, they settled down in Layton, Utah as a high school math and physics teacher and a soccer coach at Syracuse High School. After 5 comfortable years there, Bill and Jessica got the impression that it was time to move on. They decided that they would move from Utah with their 4 young boys (ages 4 mo. - 7 yrs.) to Missouri so that he could complete a doctoral program in mathematics education. They loved their 4 years in Missouri, and after graduating with his Ph.D. they moved to Gilbert Arizona so that Bill could teach at Arizona State University (ASU). It was there in Gilbert that their 5th child and only daughter joined their family. Through teaching and researching at ASU and working with teachers across the country, Bill discovered that his passion still was centered in teaching math and teaching math teachers how to reach all students. Bill and Jessica decided to move across the country again as Bill took a position at Valdosta State University in South Georgia so that he could focus more on teaching math teachers and less on conducting original research. They arrived in Georgia amid the height of the COVID-19 shutdowns, which led to a slow start settling down in Georgia. They grew to love Georgia and were planning to be there for a long time. But God had other plans. Through a series of miraculous events, Bill and Jessica were led back across the country (for hopefully the last cross-country move) to Rexburg, Idaho. Bill is now a member of the Mathematics Department at BYU-Idaho. He has found his dream job in which he can teach math, teach future math teachers, and testify of the goodness of God and power of Jesus Christ.

name: Blaine Call
image_alt: A professional photo of Adjunct Faculty Blaine Call.

sections.Description:
My adventures in art started out the same as most kids, coloring with crayons and drawing on scrap paper. I suffered through art class in Jr. High School, but once I got to high school I got excited about art and have been drawing and painting ever since. In college I started to realize some of the opportunities that art would offer me in life. I pursued a degree in illustration and was in my last year of studies when a fellow artist convinced me to take some education classes to be a teacher. Originally against this idea I did not, but with a little persuasion I relented and took the education classes. I graduated and also obtained my teaching credentials and took a job teaching high school.

As a teacher I have had a lot of freedom to explore and experiment in many areas of art. Teaching gave me the opportunity to constantly draw and paint. Also, I did ceramic pottery and sculpture, painted sets for plays, painted murals, taught traditional and digital photography classes, did graphic design, taught art history, and also learned to work in stained glass.

As a public education teacher, I found it necessary to have a little more income, which led me to obtaining my master’s degree in illustration. I began working in the evenings for the College of Southern Idaho and now for BYU Idaho. Teaching at the college level has been rewarding for me as a teacher and I value the time I get to spend with the student as they explore their art interests.

This journey that my interest in art has taken me on has been both rewarding and challenging, but one I would not change for the world.

name: Brian Brown
image_alt: A professional photo of Adjunct Faculty Brian Brown.

sections.Biography:
Brian was born and raised in Idaho Falls. As a youngster he was drawn to the artistic side of life and bucked the trend of family engineers by becoming a photographer. He attended BYU and Ricks college and graduated with a degree in Art. After graduation he opened Brown Photography, a commercial based studio that gave him the excitement he desired, where nothing was ever the same, and each new job was a challenge and a new learning experience.

Brian is a PPA Master of Photography and a PPA certified Photographer. He has been active in Professional Photographers of Idaho as a board member and past president. He has been Master Photographer of the Year 3 separate times and has numerous awards including multiple Fuji and Kodak Gallery awards.

His creative side carries over into other areas of his life as well. He enjoys woodturning and creating unique forms and shapes. He also enjoys the beauty of outdoors. Teaching

has been a great blessing helping those who are passionate and excited about photography. Like any other profession, Art requires a lot of dedication and work to excel, and it is rewarding to see former students rise to the occasion.

sections.Biography: I was introduced to graphic design through a required lettering class for art majors at Ricks College, which jumpstarted my love for all things typography. After graduating with my BFA in graphic design, I worked in the design industry for fourteen years, first in environmental graphic design for clients such as the Kennedy Space Center, Warner Brothers, and Disney (including work for the virtual theme park DisneyQuest, now the subject of a Defunctland episode), and then overseeing the in-house design team at BYU-Idaho. I became a faculty member for the BYU-Idaho Art Department in 2010 and love learning about and teaching UX/UI design, typography, art history (especially the history of graphic design, illustration, and photography), and developing creativity and curiosity.

name: Bruce Richards

sections.Description:
Bruce Richards grew up on a family Jersey farm and served as a missionary in Barcelona, Spain. He received a bachelor’s and master’s degree in Dairy Science from Utah State University, participating on the university’s first Dairy Challenge team. Upon completion of his master’s degree, he attended the University of Illinois, where he studied strategies to prevent fatty liver in dairy cows and obtained a PhD in Animal Science.

Brother Richards spent the next 11.5 years teaching Animal Nutrition and Dairy Science courses at Delaware Valley University in Doylestown, PA. While at Delaware Valley, Brother Richards coached the university’s Dairy Challenge team. In August of 2022 Brother Richards started at Utah State University as the Dairy Extension Specialist. When the opportunity came to return to the classroom and teach full-time at BYU-Idaho, Brother Richards took it starting in the fall of 2024. He teaches Dairy Production, Animal Nutrition, and other courses as needed, and coaches the BYUI Dairy Challenge team.

He has performed with Broadway Touring Companies and as backup musician with many well known artists. He soloed with the Utah Symphony, the Orchestra at Temple Square and throughout Taiwan, China, and Hong Kong. He maintains an active performing schedule as a backup musician, soloist, and clinician.

sections.Bio:
CJ has been teaching online for BYU-Idaho since 2011 when he began as an online instructor while still working full-time in healthcare. In 2015, he became a full-time faculty member at BYU-Idaho.

Prior to teaching full-time he worked full-time as a healthcare compliance professional for Intermountain Healthcare, University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, the University of Texas System and as Chief Compliance Officer for an international medical device company.

CJ has a passion for teaching and has developed curricula and taught adult employees seeking national medical coding and compliance certifications, trade workshops, seminars, and university courses.

In addition to his medical degree from the University of Illinois at Chicago College of Medicine, CJ holds a Master of Education (M.Ed.) from the University of Texas at Brownsville. He completed his B.S., magna cum laude, from Brigham Young University, Provo, UT.

CJ also holds the following professional certifications:

name: Camille Cureton
image_alt: A portrait photo of Camille Cureton

sections.Description:
Before joining BYUI, Camille Cureton dedicated 29 years to public education, with experience spanning various school districts such as Sugar Salem, Jefferson, West Jefferson, and Notus. Her instructional background encompasses teaching across grades 1-8, complemented by administrative roles overseeing Preschool through 12th grade and online high school and alternative high school programs.

Camille completed her education with an associate degree from Ricks College and a bachelor’s degree from Lewis Clark State College. She continued her studies at Northwest Nazarene University, where she obtained a master’s degree in Educational Leadership (M.Ed.). She later pursued additional education, earning an Education Specialist (Ed.S.) degree.

Beyond her professional pursuits, Camille embraces the role of a proud parent to three children and two daughters-in-law, and a grandparent to three grandchildren. She and her husband love to travel, explore culinary “First Bites,” and cherish valuable moments with their family—no matter where they are.

name: Chris Allison

sections.Biography:
Let’s start with the best part first, my wife. I am married to my beautiful wife, Rochelle. Together we have three daughters and many grandchildren. I love being a grandpa! I love spending time with my grandchildren! I tell my daughters that their children are my grandchildren first, and their children second. That is the priority ranking.

I spent 24 years in the Army Reserves and National Guard. For part of that time I was in the 19 th Group Special Forces, where I got to play with some very fun toys and jump out of a lot of airplanes and helicopters, even some jets! After retiring from the military, I spent 12 years part-time with Madison Fire Department in Rexburg, Idaho as an Advanced EMT, structure firefighter, and wildland firefighter.

I love to travel and have led tours to Europe, Central America, and Alaska. I make it a priority to visit Yellowstone and Alaska every summer.

sections.Description:
Chris Andrews graduated from Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah, with a bachelor's degree in business management. He continued his graduate studies at the University of Utah, earning an MBA in finance, followed by a doctorate degree in instructional design for online learning from Idaho State University.

name: Craig Lindstrom

sections.Description:
Craig Lindstrom graduated from the University of Utah with a bachelor's degree in business management. He then completed a master's degree in information systems from Utah State University.

Craig worked as an assistant professor at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah, and at BYU in Provo, Utah. He returned to UVU in 2013 to serve as a lecturer while operating his self-employed business Sage Enterprises, offering high-tech training and consulting to individuals and companies. In 2016, he joined the faculty in the Department of Computer Information and Technology at BYU-Idaho.

name: Dallin Hansen

sections.Description:
Dr. Dallin Hansen holds a DMA degree in violin performance from Arizona State University, studying with Dr. Katherine McLin. His doctoral work included studies with Arnold Steinhardt and Ida Kavafian in master class settings and chamber music with Mark Steinberg. Dr. Hansen also earned a M.M. degree in Orchestral Conducting, studying with Kory Katseanes, and a B.M. degree in Music Education, both from Brigham Young University. Principal teachers include Katherine McLin, Gerald Elias, Donna Fairbanks, and LaMar Barrus.

Dr. Hansen has performed as a solo artist throughout Utah, Idaho and Arizona. His orchestral and chamber music experience includes performance tours of Europe and Russia with the BYU Chamber Orchestra, performances with the Utah Symphony, and first violinist of the ASU Chamber Players (ASU's top mixed chamber ensemble). Dr. Hansen directs the string pedagogy program, teaches applied violin, and performs with the Serenata Strings faculty quartet at BYU-Idaho.

name: Daniel Kerr

sections.Description: Dr. Daniel Kerr is the Director of Organ Studies and oversees the Musicianship program at BYU-Idaho. He also coordinates the BYU-Idaho Hymn Festival, which commissions new hymn texts and tunes each year. He received his bachelor's, master's and Doctor of Musical Arts degrees from the University of Southern California Thornton School of Music, where he studied organ with Dr. Ladd Thomas and Professor Cherry Rhodes. Prior to his appointment at BYU-Idaho, he taught at USC and at California State University Los Angeles, was accompanist for the Claremont Chorale, Musical Director of the Foothill Summer Theatre, and Organist and handbell choir director at Pasadena Presbyterian Church. He has performed with the Los Angeles Philharmonic Orchestra as well as at various conventions of the American Guild of Organists (2004 National Convention, 2011 Northwest Regional Convention, and the 2017 West Regional Convention). He was a soloist for the 2008 Eccles Organ Recital Series at Salt Lake’s Cathedral of the Madeleine, and is a regular recitalist on the organs of Temple Square in Salt Lake City. He is an Associate of the American Guild of Organists and is currently the dean of the Eastern Idaho Chapter of the AGO.

sections.Description:
Daniel Stoker graduated from BYU-Idaho in 2006 with a bachelor's degree in social studies teacher education. He gained an additional degree from Brigham Young University in Arabic, followed by a master's degree in Middle East studies in 2012 from the American University in Cairo.

Daniel taught social studies classes at Othello High School in Washington State for two years and served as a program assistant at BYU helping studies with Arabic studies. name: Darren Clark
image_alt: A professional photo of Faculty Darren Clark.

sections.Description:
Darren Clark earned a BFA in studio art from Utah State University. He earned an MFA in photography from Louisiana State University. Darren has been teaching at BYU-Idaho since 2000. He currently teaches Photography and Introduction to Visual Arts. He grew up in Eastern Idaho and has a strong connection with the landscape and inhabitants of the region. This connection to place is what drives a lot of his photographic projects. His current photographic obsession is making photographs of sparse/empty landscapes as part of a long-term project on quiet places. Darren is also an obsessed birdwatcher. He spends his free time looking for and photographing birds and their habitat. Ultimately, birdwatching and photography are excuses to spend time outside experiencing beauty. Darren and his wife Susan have three sons (and one daughter-in-law).

name: Dave Rowe

sections.Description:
Dave Rowe graduated from BYU-Idaho in 2009 with a bachelor's degree Business Management: Marketing and Advertising. He continued his graduate studies at Navenn Jindal School of Management-University of Texas at Dallas, where he earned a master's degree in Marketing, specializing in digital advertising and marketing track.

Professor Rowe has held many positions in the marketing industry, including account coordinator, marketing specialist, paid search specialist, digital marketing and advertising lead, and marketing manager for several industry leading companies.

In 2019, he joined the faculty in the Department of Marketing at BYU-Idaho. He teaches courses on marketing analysis, web business creation, social media marketing, integrated business core, and career preparation.

In 2022, Dave became a fractional marketing leader for Groweth Marketing, LLC, and offers sound marketing advice and strategies for companies seeking to grow.

name: David Olsen

sections.Description: Dr. David Olsen teaches voice at Brigham Young University-Idaho, where he also serves as the Director the Vocal Studies. An avid performer, Dr. Olsen has performed in a wide variety of styles and venues, from musical theatre to opera, barbershop to acapella jazz. Some of his recent appearances include the title role inJulius Caesar, Papageno in The Magic Flute, the Father in Hansel and Gretel, and the baritone/bass soloist in Brahms's German Requiem, Mozart'sRequiem, and Handel's Messiah. Other professional engagements include several seasons with the Utah Festival Opera Young Artist program, appearing as featured soloist with the Tulsa Signature Symphony, and recording with the Boston-based early music ensemble La Donna Musicale. He has also been featured as a soloist in multiple works from the BYU-Idaho Sacred Music Series, including Robert Cundick's God's Everlasting Love and Newell Dayley's Bring Forth My Zion. Dr. Olsen received his associate's degree from Ricks College, his bachelor's degree from Utah State University, and his master's and doctoral degrees from the University of Oklahoma.

sections.Biography: I was born and raised in Salt Lake City, Utah and I originally went to Southern Utah University to become a high school mathematics teacher. While at SUU, I was baptized a member of the LDS church. After college however, I decided to forgo teaching school and further my experience working as a mathematician and statistician for various contractors at Hill Air Force Base. While there, I married Penny Meyerink and we moved to Ogden, Utah, where we lived for the next 29 years. We are the parents of 9 children and currently 26 grandchildren with 2 more on the way. While in Ogden, I went to Utah State University and received my master’s degree. After 6 years at Hill Air Force Base, I changed employment to ATK Thiokol, where I performed reliability studies on the space shuttle booster motors, as well as several weapon systems. While in Ogden, a perfect storm hit the school district and most of the mathematics teachers left during one school year. Because I had several children in the school district, I left Thiokol and became a math teacher, which was where I should have been anyway. I spent the next 10 years teaching math, serving 2 of those years as a high school principal. In 2014, my daughter was attending BYUI and informed me of a job opening for a mathematics professor. I applied for the job and living on faith, my wife and I moved to Rigby, Idaho and bought a house. We have lived there since and absolutely love the Eastern Idaho area.

He is the father of 6 children, grandfather of 11, and happily married to Tracie, a cute vivacious third-grade teacher.

sections.Bio: Diedre Sakota is a dance educator, choreographer, and performer. In her youth, she had the privilege of dancing with two pre-professional dance companies, Dance in Flight and Ricochet Modern Dance Company. She received her ballet training from Barbara Wilson and was awarded Distinction in her Royal Academy of Dance examinations. Her performing repertoire includes variations from Swan Lake, Sleeping Beauty, Nutcracker, Beauty and the Beast, and many modern/contemporary works. While pursuing her undergrad at BYU-Idaho, Diedre had the opportunity to perform with Dance Alliance and toured Ecuador, Peru, Russia, Canada, and the United States. After graduating in 2009, she married the love of her life and became the mother of four beautiful children. In 2014, Diedre founded Aspire Dance Company in Meridian, Idaho, and collaborated on a benefit concert for Mountain States Tumor Institute. In 2016, she joined The Dance Collaborative of Idaho Falls and became co-Artistic Director. Diedre has taught for several dance studios and universities, namely University of Idaho, Clark College, and BYU-Idaho. She has a passion for health education and teaches PE for the Oneida school district. In 2021, she graduated from Middlesex University with a Master of Arts in dance technique pedagogy. Her thesis research included ethnographic and phenomenological perspectives in dance pedagogy. She is currently a Ph.D. candidate in Kinesiology from Concordia University, St. Paul.

name: Donnie Tapp
image_alt: A professional photo of Adjunct Faculty Donnie Tapp.

sections.Biography: Donnie Tapp grew up in Eastern Idaho, where he learned to value the rural landscape and appreciate the character of the many small towns in the area. As a youth his parents encouraged him to cultivate a love for drawing, and near the beginning of his undergraduate study at Brigham Young University-Idaho he began seriously considering a career in the arts. He earned a bachelors degree in Studio Art in 2014, dividing his time between sculpture, photography, and painting. In 2021 Donnie earned an MFA in oil painting from Academy of Art University. His work expresses his feelings for the landscape of his childhood home, where he has returned back to as an adult and enjoyed experiencing in a new light. He currently lives in Idaho Falls with his wife, Jamie, and daughters McKinley and Olivia.

sections.Description:
Duane Adamson completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Utah with a bachelor's degree in political science. He then earned as master's degree at Utah State University in political science and completed doctorate work in foreign affairs from the University of Virginia.

Duane was an active part of the Mike Leavitt for Governor Campaign in the early 1990s as an area director. He then worked in the Utah Governor's Office as a deputy for communications. After completing his graduate work, he filled several professorships at James Madison University, BYU, and the University of Virginia. In 2006 he joined the faculty in the Department of History, Geography, and Political Science at BYU-Idaho. In 2014 he accepted a position in the College of Language and Letters at BYU-Idaho, serving as an associate dean for professional development and mentored student research. He filled the role of department chair in the Department of History, Geography, and Political Science from 2018 to 2024.

She studied voice with Michael Ballam and attended voice workshops of Richard Miller and Clayne Robison.

sections.Bio: Gary Larsen is a professional dancer, teacher, and choreographer specializing in world and percussive dance forms. He holds a Masters Degree in Dance from UCLA and a PhD in Ethnochoreology (Sociocultural Anthropology of dance) from the University of Limerick in Ireland. As a performer, he has traveled to dozens of countries as both group member and soloist. He has taught and created choreography for workshops, performing groups, and schools throughout the United States and in numerous other countries for over 20 years. He is a Professor of Dance at Brigham Young University-Idaho where he oversees and/or teaches courses in clogging, tap, world dance, dance history, theory, philosophy, humanities, choreography, and performance. In his spare time, he owns and directs a dance company that travels the world performing American traditional and vernacular dance with his wife and three children.

name: Gregory Angus

Education: MHA
sections.Bio:
As a BYU-Idaho healthcare administration graduate himself (graduated 2012), Greg has enjoyed returning to the university and teaching many of the classes he took as a student years ago. Greg’s experience at BYU-Idaho as a student was life-changing, so when the opportunity to return as a faculty member presented itself in 2019, it was an easy career choice for him and his family to make.

Before returning to BYU-Idaho, Greg worked at several large academic medical centers throughout the country. Most recently he was the Administrator over several surgical and medical specialties at University of Colorado Health (UCHealth). Prior to that role, he spent a couple of years doing similar work at University of Wisconsin Health (UW Health), in addition to completing a two-year Administrative Fellowship at the organization. Greg earned a Master of Health Administration (MHA) degree from Penn State University where he completed an Administrative Residency within the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) health system.

Greg and his wife Jess have four kids. In his free time, he enjoys running, biking, playing sports and being outdoors. He also likes to spend time reading, completing home improvement projects and spending quality time with his family.

sections.Biography: I have always enjoyed mathematics, it has not always been easy but it has been fun. In high school I took extra math classes as electives. As an undergrad I selected math as my major and I planned on doing something with applied math. During my last semester I needed one more math class and the only one that was available was a capstone math education class, because of that class I fell in love with the idea of teaching math. I have struggled through some math classes, and this was one of the strengths that I think I bring to the math class room. I know what it feels like to be confused and to have to put in the extra work to understand the concepts. My graduate work included creating technology enhanced lesson plans for secondary mathematics education and research in the area of example generation in the calculus classroom. I love sharing with students my love for math. Most often my classroom is busy with students at the board working together to figure out new concepts and practice skills.

Dr. Higginbotham has published a large variety of scholarly articles for various research publications.

name: Jack LaBaugh

sections.Description:
Jack LaBaugh studied at Ricks College before graduating from Idaho State University with a bachelor's degree in mass communications, public relations, and advertising. He continued his graduate studies at Brigham Young University, earning master's degree in mass communication and media studies in 2003.

Brother LaBaugh began working at BYU-Idaho in 2001 as a multimedia and print publication adviser. He oversaw the university newspaper and multimedia yearbooks. He then worked in academic publishing sales with Cengage Learning in Salt Lake City, Utah, and later as an editorial director over marketing at Melaleuca, Inc. During this time, Brother LaBaugh continued to work at BYU-Idaho as a faculty member in the Department of Communication. He now also serves as a faculty member in the Department of Marketing.

1999 | Bachelor's of Arts, Mass Communications Public Relations and Advertising; Minor in Political Science, Idaho State University
1997 | Associate Degree in Arts and Sciences, Print Journalism, Ricks College

sections.Biography:
I am originally from Oregon but have lived all over the country; I am an avid traveler and have backpacked through different countries in the north and south hemispheres of the world. In my free time, I spend time with my husband and two girls; we have a lot of fun together, and we try to practice the advice from the Proclamation of the Family regarding wholesome recreation; I run so that I can maintain the habit of eating chocolate! I love the gospel. It has been my light in the darkness, and I love teaching the students at BYUI. They are my favorite part of this profession!

Started teaching at BYU-Idaho in June of 2008.

sections.Description:
Jedd Walker attended Brigham Young University before graduating from the University of Utah with a bachelor's of science in architecture. He then completed a master's degree architecture at the University of Utah in 1999.

Jedd has extensive commercial experience in construction and architecture. He worked as a job captain for BBSA in Salt Lake City, Utah, overseeing site design, development, specifications, and more. He then served as a project manager and managing architect for CRSA for six years. Jedd joined the faculty in the Department of Design and Construction Management at BYU-Idaho in 2006. He has also served as assistant campus architect, campus architect, and director of architecture and planning services.

He received his Bachelor of Science in history at Brigham Young University Idaho and a master’s in educational administration from Southwest Baptist University in Missouri.

Jeffrey Meservy attended Ricks College before graduating from the University of Utah with a bachelor's degree in political science. He continued his graduate studies at Brigham Young University, earning a master's degree in public administration, followed by a juris doctorate degree in law from Purdue Global Law School.

Brother Meservy has served in the Church Education System since 1991, where he has taught students as a seminary teacher, seminary principal, pre-service trainer, manager, institute director, and adjunct professor at BYU. He joined the faculty in the Department of Religious Education at BYU-Idaho in 2005.

"The Willie and Martin Handcart Companies: Application and Insights into a Recurring Rescue" ( BYU Religious Educator, Vo. 17, No. 3, [2016])

name: Jennifer Jones

sections.Bio: Jennifer Jones received her Ph.D. in Special Education from the University of Utah, her M.Ed. in Early Childhood Studies from Boise State University, and her B.S. in Early Childhood/Special Education from BYU-Idaho. She started teaching at BYU-Idaho in 2022. Before this, she was a Career Line Assistant Professor at the University of Utah, supervising early childhood special education candidates in their fieldwork and student teaching experiences in early childhood classrooms. She was also an Assistant Professor at Purdue University Northwest, where she taught courses in early childhood and special education programs and conducted research about teacher preparation and partnering with families. She taught in public schools as a special education preschool teacher and elementary school teacher. She enjoys hiking, riding her bike, and downhill skiing in her free time.

Jessica Mecham graduated from Brigham Young University with a bachelor's degree in music. She continued her graduate studies at the Northwesten UNiversity, where she earned a master's degree in music history and literature. Then she returned to BYU and gained a second master's degree in library and music. Finally, she completed a doctorate degree in humanities from Faulkner University.

Dr. Mecham has served as an adjunct professor for Salt Lake Community College and the College of Southern Idaho. She Also lent her corporate research talents to ComUnity Lending, a mortgage banking firm in California. In 2002, she was working as an online professor at Century College when she joined the faculty in the Department of Humanities and Philosophy at BYU-Idaho. In addition to teaching students, Dr. Mecham also serves as a Faculty Association College Representative fo r the university's Faculty Association Board. Dr. Mecham currently provides online teaching for Southern New Hampshire University, along with her services to BYU-Idaho.

sections.Description:
Jody Swenson attended Northern Montana College before graduating from Montana State University with a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering. He continued his graduate studies at Utah State University, where he earned a master's degree and a doctorate degree in electrical engineering.

Dr. Sweson has worked closely with Campbell Scientific as a senior electrical Engineer for over 30 years. He currently serves as a faculty member in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at BYU-Idaho.

name: Joelle Moen
image_alt: A portrait photo of Joelle Moen

sections.Description:
Joelle Moen has three degrees in English—a B.A. from Brigham Young University and an M.A. and PhD from Washington State University. She specializes in American literature, especially twentieth century and African American literatures. Her PhD dissertation centered on the response of African American writers (Chesnutt, Hurston, and Johnson) to the legacy of the pseudoscientific categorization of people according to race.

In 2018-19, Professor Moen served as a Fulbright Roving Scholar of American Literature and Culture in Norway. In this role she served as a traveling guest lecturer, giving workshops with topics that included Jim Crow laws and culture, rhetorical devices in the “Letter from Birmingham Jail,” decoding propaganda, revision strategies for writers, and various American literary and historical texts. She visited 81 schools and taught nearly 300 teachers some 9500 students. Since then, she has served on the Fulbright National Screening Committee for English Teaching Assistants.

Dr. Moen’s life was changed by a study abroad program to London, where she learned the wonders of studying art and culture. Since then, she’s visited all 50 of the United States and traveled to more than 40 countries outside the U.S.: Canada, Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, Brazil, Argentina, Peru, Bolivia, Australia, China, Hong Kong, India, Nepal, Israel, Turkiye, the United Kingdom (Northern Ireland, Scotland, England, Wales), Ireland, Spain, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Poland, Austria, Slovenia, Slovakia, Hungary, Czech Republic, Croatia, Italy, Greece, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Republic of South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Russia (then the Soviet Union).

name: John Fisher
image_alt: A professional photo of Associate Dean John Timothy Fisher

sections.Description:
John Fisher is an associate dean in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at BYU-Idaho, and also serves as a faculty member in the Department of Biology.

John attended Utah Valley University and Brigham Young University before graduating from Utah State University with a bachelor's degree in chemistry and biochemistry. He continued his graduate studies at the University of Iowa, where he earned a doctorate degree in anatomy and cell biology.

Dr. Fisher has worked as a acturial technician for Transamerica and an associate professor of biological sciences at Snow College in Ephraim, Utah. He joined the Department of Biology at BYU-Idaho in 2015. He has served as an associate dean of student success in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences since 2019.

"The Pillars of Making Critical Decisions Correctly" (BYU-Idaho Devotional, July 9, 2024)

sections.Description: Jon Klein is Professor of Horn and Coordinator of Brass Studies at BYU-Idaho. Since joining the faculty in 2010 he has taught Introduction to Music, Brass Methods, Brass Literature, Brass Pedagogy, and has conducted the Brass Choir and Symphony Band. Dr. Klein studied music performance at the San Francisco Conservatory of Music and Boston University. He completed a Doctor of Musical Arts degree at the University of Utah in 2012. Primary teachers include horn soloist Eric Ruske, Robert Ward of the San Francisco Symphony, Philip Munds of the Baltimore Symphony, and Stephen Proser of the Utah Symphony. As an active performer and chamber musician, Dr. Klein is a member of the BYU-I Faculty Brass and Wind quintets. Additionally he has performed with the Utah Symphony, Utah Chamber Orchestra/Ballet West, Boise Philharmonic, Billings Symphony and the Spokane Symphony.

sections.Biography:
Josh Hobbs was raised on a farm in Franklin, Idaho. He was fortunate to have a family that encouraged his interest in the visual arts, being influenced by family members who often made art with him.

Josh and his wife, Annie, have five children and reside in Teton, Idaho.

name: Joshua Abegglen
image_alt: A professional photo of Department Chair Joshua Abegglen.

sections.Personal Biography::
During Joshua Abegglen’s childhood in St. Anthony, Idaho, Saturday morning cartoons played a big influence. He knew at a young age that he wanted to visually tell stories and create animated characters. Having remained singular in this vision, he feels there really weren’t any other career options for him. Josh’s art is diverse, as he works with a variety of different mediums. His art is informed by a natural curiosity and a desire to work through problems. Viewing art as something of a puzzle, Brother Abegglen takes immense satisfaction in working through the processes necessary to solve those puzzles. He’s recently been taken with the idea of art being transformative, which has led him to lutherie (designing and building stringed instruments). He loves the idea of his art becoming a tool in someone else’s hands to make more art. Brother Abegglen greatly enjoys teaching at BYU-I, as he studied here when it transitioned from Ricks College to BYU-Idaho. One of his favorite things about teaching here is the coupling of the gospel and learning about art; he wanted to come back and be a part of that process.

If there is one thing Joshua Abegglen wished all students knew, it would be the following: “Be observant to everything around you. Life is so interesting, and there are so many things to draw inspiration from. Try to pay attention to those seemingly small details and take note of them in journals or sketchbooks. Ask questions about what you are observing and look for answers to those questions; they are fuel for creativity”.

sections.Biography:
Justin Bates is an actor and educator who has worked throughout the Rocky Mountain region of the United States and Canada for most of his career. He earned his B.S. in Theatre from Southern Utah University and an M.F.A. in Acting from the University of Montana. Justin has taught in several academic and pre-professional training programs, including the University of Montana, Utah Tech University in St. George, Utah, and the University of Louisiana at Lafayette.

A student-centered teacher, Justin joined the faculty of Brigham Young University–Idaho in 2009, where he teaches courses such as Introduction to Theatre, Voice and Diction, Storytelling, and all levels of Acting. In addition to directing annually as part of the department's mainstage production season, Justin has served as Associate Dean for Online Instruction in the College of Performing and Visual Arts and as Chair of the Department of Theatre and Dance from 2019 to 2024.

Justin is a collaborative, honest, and compassionate artist whose directing and acting interests range from Shakespeare and Absurdism to Realism and Magical Realism. Known for his strong ensemble work, some of Justin’s directing credits include the world premiere of Jon Jory’s adaptation of Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey , A Midsummer Night’s Dream , Mary Stuart (honored by Region 7 of the Kennedy Center American College Theatre Festival), Dancing at Lughnasa , Enchanted April , Waiting for Godot , The Tempest , How I Learned to Drive , The House of Bernarda Alba (in an original translation by award-winning translator Steven J. Stewart), Silent Sky , Leaving Eden (an original work by Janine Gilbert based on the award-winning short stories by Jack Harrell), These Shining Lives , Blithe Spirit , and Babette’s Feast .

name: Kelsie Carter

sections.Biography: Meet Kelsie; an educator, creator, performer, and dance enthusiast. Kelsie currently owns and directs her dance studio, Dancer’s Edge Rexburg. She also has the privilege of teaching as adjunct faculty in the Dance Department at Brigham Young University-Idaho. Kelsie is passionate about challenging and encouraging her students to unlock their best work and find bliss in their movement journey. Kelsie loves connecting and collaborating with peers and students choreographically and technically. Kelsie received her BA in Dance from BYU-Idaho in 2017 and danced semi-professionally for two years after her schooling with The Dance Collaborative. Kelsie has received her YTT-200 certification with Yoga Alliance, PBT Certification, Above the BARRE certification, and is currently pursuing an MA in Dance with a concentration in education from Texas Woman's University. When Kelsie is not dancing or teaching, she enjoys traveling, eating as many desserts as possible (brownies are her favorite), and spending time with family and friends.

name: Kerry Moser
image_alt: A professional photo of Adjunct Faculty Kerry Moser.

sections.Biography: Kerry Moser has always loved Art. As young girl, she commandeered an old cinderblock building on the family farm in Gooding, Idaho and turned it into her makeshift art studio, where oil was her primary medium. In high school, Kerry decided to make her living as a photographer, and with that resolved, she bought her first camera. Since there were no photography classes at her high school, it wasn’t until college when she received any real instruction, and she has been hooked ever since. After graduating with a degree in Photography, Kerry worked as a professional portrait photographer for 20 years. After her children got a little older, Kerry returned to BYUI to earn a degree in Art Education and then taught Art and Photography in the public school system for eleven years. A special passion for Kerry has been exploring the interplay of light and shadow and how they communicate or distort form. Kerry and her husband, Leon, have four children and one grandchild and reside in Sugar City, Idaho.
Education: Bachelor of Science in Art Education, Brigham Young University-Idaho 2010
Associate of Art and Science in Photography, Ricks College1991

name: Kevin Meyer

sections.Description:
Dr. Kevin Meyer is a versatile percussionist from Sioux Falls, South Dakota and is currently the Director of Percussion at Brigham Young University - Idaho (BYUI) and also the Principal Percussionist in the Idaho Falls Symphony.

Prior to his appointment at BYUI he was the principal percussionist in the United States Naval Academy Band (USNAB). During his tenure (2008-2020) in the USNAB he performed in the Concert Band, Brass Ensemble, marching/ceremonial units, chamber winds, and drumset in the Commandant’s Combo, Superintendent’s Jazz Combo, Navy Blues and Gold Blues Band, Riptide Jazz Ensemble, and the Crabtowne Stompers New Orleans style band. He has also performed at the International Tuba Euphonium Conference in Malaga, Spain, Knoxville, TN, Tempe, AZ, and multiple regional ITEC festivals.

Dr. Meyer has performed as a soloist with the United States Naval Academy Band, Indiana University Wind Ensemble, Tar River Symphonic Band, ECU Percussion Ensemble, Snow College Percussion Ensemble, and the BYU - Provo Percussion Ensemble. He was the winner of the 2001 Utah Percussive Arts Society Rudimental Snare Drum Solo Competition, and has performed in clinics at the International Association of Jazz Educators and Percussive Arts Society International Convention.

Dr. Meyer has received a Doctor of Musical Arts degree from the University of Maryland, College Park; a Master of Music in Percussion Performance from East Carolina University; and a Bachelor of Music Education from Brigham Young University, Provo. description:

name: Kristi Ballif

sections.Description: Kristi Ballif earned her Master of Music degree in Flute Performance from Arizona State University and her Bachelor of Music in Flute Performance from Brigham Young University. Since then, she has taught flute at Brigham Young University-Idaho and Colorado Mesa University. Kristi won the National Flute Association Convention Performer's Competition in 2012 and has been a guest for the Temple Square Artist Series and the Mormon Tabernacle Choir. She has also played with the Grand Junction Symphony Orchestra and the Western Colorado Flute Choir. Kristi is the author of Music Theory for the Flutist, a theory book designed especially for flute students. As a clinician, she has presented for the National Flute Association Convention, the Colorado Flute Association, the Colorado Music Educator's Association Convention, and the Gateway Canyons Lecture Series. In addition to her classical flute studies, Kristi enjoys playing the Irish flute and Highland Bagpipes.

sections.Description: Kyle Johnson graduated from BYU-Idaho in Elementary Education (2012). He has a deep passion for reading and early literacy. He taught third grade in Madison School District for seven years. Kyle received a master's in educational leadership from Northwestern Nazarene University (2018). He became a literacy Coach and Federal Programs Coordinator for West Jefferson School District (2020). He continued those responsibilities and also became the Principal for Terreton and Hamer Elementary Schools (2021-2024). While at West Jefferson he was also given opportunities to be a basketball and a Track and Field Coach. Kyle over the years has been on many BYU-Idaho advisory boards in the education department, and recently was the local practitioner for BYU-Idaho’s AAQEP Accreditation. Kyle has four amazing kids who like him, love all things sports, especially running. He is excited to be here to be a part of preparing future educators to become Leaders and Disciples of Christ.

name: Laurana Roderer

sections.Description:
Dr. Laurana Wheeler Roderer is a violinist whose playing is an engaging blend of intuition and intellect, and she is establishing herself as an artist who “colors outside the lines” by presenting uniquely curated programs meant to connect audiences with the natural world and with each other. Laurana grew up fiddling and participating in local competitions in her home state of Idaho, and she discovered a passion for classical music in high school under the tutelage of Emma Rubinstein. She then went on to complete her undergraduate degree in violin performance at Utah State University, where she studied with Robert Waters and the Fry Street Quartet.

In 2022 she graduated with a Master’s degree in violin performance from Arizona State University, where she also completed her Doctorate of Musical Arts in 2024. An active performer and educator, Laurana is the Assistant Concertmaster of the Idaho State-Civic Symphony, and she also teaches as adjunct violin faculty at Brigham Young University-Idaho.

name: Lonna Joy Smoot

sections.Lonna Joy Smoot:
Lonna Joy Smoot earned her Bachelor of Arts Degree in Music Education with an emphasis in Choral Education from Utah State University and a Masters Degree in Vocal Performance from Brigham Young University.She was a recipient of the Marie Eccles Caine Music Scholarship at Utah State University and a recipient of the Ariel Bybee Award, at Brigham Young University.

She was awarded a Graduate Vocal Assistantship at BYU and studied voice with Lawrence Vincent and Clayne Robison during her studies in Provo. In 2003, Smoot was selected to be a guest lecturer at the International Colloquium for Vernacular, Hispanic, Historical, American and Folklore Studies held in Puebla, Mexico.

Lonna Joy has performed in recitals and concerts in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Austria, Italy, Finland, and Russia. After graduation from Utah State University, she studied with the Cultural Studies Academy in conjunction with Baldwin Wallace College in Salzburg, Austria with Rainer Buland of the Mozarteum. Following studies at BYU she was a participated in the American Institute of Musical Studies in Graz, Austria.

Some of her operatic credits include; Despina in Così fan tutte , Concepcion in L’heure Espagnole, The Witch Hänsel and Gretel, the Countess in Le Nozze de Figaro, Gretel in Hänsel and Gretel, Mimí in La Boheme, the First Lady in Die Zauberflöte, the Monitor in Suor Angelica, Gianetta in The Gondoliers, and the Mother in Menotti’s Amahl and the Night Visitors. Smoot has also performed in productions of Otello, Three Hermits, I Pagliacci, and Carmen with Utah Opera. Enjoying opportunities in musical theater productions, Lonna Joy has more recently performed such roles as Mrs. Lovett in Sondheim’s Sweeney Todd, Golde in Fiddler on The Roof, and Miss Hannigan in Annie.

For the past 12 years, she has enjoyed performing with the Idaho Falls Opera Theatre and is also a regular soloist in their autumn concerts. She sings with Anam Cara (The Chamber Choir of Idaho), currently under the direction of Dr. Kevin Brower of BYU-Idaho. Smoot is a member of the Idaho Falls Opera Theatre board of directors and Anam Cara board of directors. Lonna Joy is a current certified music teacher in the State of Idaho. In 2012, she began serving as an Adjunct Faculty Member of the Music Department at BYU-Idaho.

sections.Description:
Lori Denning is a PhD candidate at Claremont Graduate University in Religion specializing in Old Testament/Hebrew. She has written a few books and just had one drop from Deseret Book titled Seeing Women in the Old Testament .

She served a mission in Barcelona, Spain. She speaks Spanish, Catalan, and can read and sing in Hebrew.

She is a native of San Diego and has a twin sister. She likes dogs, adventure sports, and all things chocolate. She is a super nerd – so much so that she once won a ComicCon trivia quiz on Star Trek.

Her favorite scripture is Alma 29:1 – O that I were an angel, and could have the wish of mine heart, that I might go forth and speak with the trump of God, with a voice to shake the earth, and cry repentance unto every people!

name: Martin Dietze-Hermosa

sections.Description:
Martin Dietze-Hermosa graduated from BYU-Idaho with a bachelor's degree in exercise physiology. His graduate studies took him to the University of Utah, where he earned a master's degree in kinesiology and exercise science. He then completed a doctorate degree in interdisciplinary health science from the University of Texas at El Paso.

Dr. Dietze-Hermosa worked professionally as a personal trainer and strength and conditioning specialist at World's Gym. He first came to BYU-Idaho as an adjunct professor in the Department of Biology in 2015. He then served as a lecturer and assistant instructor at the University of Utah and the University of Texas at El Paso as he completed his graduate studies. In 2021, he joined the faculty in the Department of Human Performance and Recreation at BYU-Idaho.

Dr. Dietze-Hermosa has co-authored over 30 research publications about human performance and strength. He also helps oversee BYU-Idaho's annual summer speed and agility camps

Education: FACHE
MBA
sections.Bio:
Matt Dixon began teaching healthcare administration at BYU Idaho in 2016. Prior to this, Matt spent 13 years as an executive with HCA Healthcare, the largest for-profit hospital operator in the United States. At HCA, Matt led the development and opening of a new hospital in Pearland, Texas, as the Chief Executive Officer of Pearland Medical Center. Under Matt’s leadership, Pearland Medical Center was recognized as one of HCA Healthcare’s highest performing hospitals in the delivery of clinical care, and employee and patient satisfaction.

Preceding his appointment at Pearland Medical Center, Matt was the Chief Operating Officer of St. Mark’s Hospital, a 315-bed tertiary level hospital in Salt Lake City, Utah. During his 7-year tenure as COO, Matt oversaw the expansion of St. Mark’s services in the areas of outpatient imaging, satellite emergency services, primary care, bariatric surgery, inpatient rehabilitation, and behavioral health.

Matt also held the position of Associate Administrator at Lakeview Hospital in Bountiful, Utah.

Matt holds a Master of Business Administration degree from the University of Michigan’s Ross School of Business and is a certified Fellow in the American College of Healthcare Executives. After graduating as the valedictorian of the David M. Kennedy Center for International Studies at Brigham Young University, Matt worked in finance and international development prior to his graduate studies. Matt is also a graduate of Ricks College, where he competed on the school’s varsity cross-county and track and field teams.

Matt was raised on his family’s farm in Jerome, Idaho and served a mission in Fresno, California. He and his wife, Anna, were married in 1996 in the Salt Lake City Temple. They are the parents of four children.

Matt loves fly fishing, hiking, backpacking, outdoor work, international travel, his wife, his kids, and a good joke.

name: Matt Moore

sections.Description: BYU-Idaho Tuba and Euphonium Facebook page
sections.Biography:
Matt Moore was born in Bountiful, Utah and spent most of his growing up years in the small town of Gypsum, Colorado. Although no one in his family was involved in music, they encouraged him to try new things. So, at the suggestion of his high school band director and young men's president, he joined the band. He started on tuba, and since he was the only tuba in the band, he quickly rose to first chair. His first lessons on brass playing were given to him by the band's baritone player.

During high school Matt was planning to become a history teacher, but after joining the band he decided to become a band director instead. Upon graduation, he attended one year of college at Western State College in Gunnison, Colorado as a music major. He then served a mission in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Upon his return, Matt attended Weber State University in Ogden, Utah. There, he finished his undergraduate degree in Music Education and student taught at Kaysville Jr. High under Randy Houtz. He studied tuba at this time with Mark Robinette. Toward the end of his undergraduate studies, Matt began playing professionally in various settings, such as pick-up orchestras, recording sessions, and as a substitute with the Utah Symphony. During this time, Matt also married his wife, Rachel, in the Salt Lake LDS Temple.

After receiving his bachelor's degree, Matt enrolled at the University of Utah to pursue a master's degree in tuba performance. There, he studied with Lee Hipp of the San Antonio Symphony and Gary Ofenloch of the Utah Symphony. During his studies, he continued to play professionally in every setting imaginable. It was also during this time that Matt began to play and record with the Orchestra at Temple Square. His playing can be heard on several Mormon Tabernacle Choir recordings. Matt has also toured with the Choir and performed on dozens of productions of Music and the Spoken Word. Matt and Rachel's first child, Annie, was born during this time in Salt Lake City.

Matt began working as a band director after completing his master's degree at the University of Utah. He taught at Bear River High School and was in charge of the school's marching, concert, and jazz band as well as beginning band at the junior high level. He continued to perform constantly during this time, specifically as substitute with the Utah Symphony, tuba player in the Brass Tacks Brass Quintet, and as principal tuba with the Orchestra at Temple Square. Matt taught band in Tremonton for three years, and Matt and Rachel had two more children, Jenna and Collin.

In the fall of 2007, Matt was hired as professor of Tuba at Brigham Young University-Idaho, where he is currently employed. From 2012 to 2014, Matt attended the prestigious Peabody Conservatory on full scholarship where he studied with Baltimore Symphony tubist, David Fedderly. While in Baltimore he performed with the Baltimore Symphony, Baltimore Symphony Brass Quintet, the Naval Academy Band Brass Quintet, and the South Florida Symphony.
