image_alt: A professional photo of Adjunct Faculty Melissa Ricks.

sections.Description:
Melissa Ricks grew up in San Luis Obispo, California but has been living in Idaho for the past 17 years, 6 of those here in Rexburg. She attended Ricks College where she received associate degrees in Elementary Education and Recreation Education. Being heavily involved and maybe a little too competitive in her awesome high school art program, she felt a little burned out with art upon beginning college. Though initially, she did not declare art as her major, she still took at least one art class per semester and loved it. After serving a missing to Guayaquil South, Ecuador, she was determined to finish her undergraduate in art. Sister Ricks received her bachelors of fine art in illustration from Brigham Young University in 2001 and was able to complete commissions for all the Church magazines at the time, a book for Deseret Book, several private commission, and sold publishing rights to Sounds of Zion to print and distribute prints or her art in various religious bookstores across the country.

Sister Ricks is a mother of five incredible kids and has loved welcoming a son in law, a daughter in law, and the cutest granddaughter into her family. After her third baby she took a seven year break from illustrating to focus on raising her kids. With her family she loves to hike, kayak, travel, bake healthy concoctions, and cheer her kids on in their sporting events. sections.Introduction:
I grew up in the Orem/Provo, Utah area (I also briefly lived in Houston, Texas) and served a mission in Eugene, Oregon. I began my higher education at Utah Valley University (UVU) studying Humanities and Art. I met my wife while we both worked in the photofinishing industry. She studied graphic design, illustration, interior design, photography, and production design at BYU. We married in 2000. I graduated with an associate degree from UVU and transferred to BYU where I studied Humanities with a History Emphasis focusing on classical studies, art history, photography, and cinema. As an undergraduate, I also worked for the Harold B. Lee Library, L. Tom Perry Special Collections preparing 19th and 20th-century publications, artwork, photographs, and film items for online access.

After graduating from BYU, I earned a master's degree in History, specializing in film history, theory, and criticism with a sub-emphasis in Greek and Roman history, at the University of Nebraska at Omaha, and completed my graduate internship for the University of Nebraska Medical Center, McGoogan Library of Medicine, Special Collections working on their photographic collections.

In 2008 I attended the University of Wisconsin-Madison briefly as a Ph.D. student in the School of Journalism and Mass Communication researching film history, theory, and criticism and working as an assistant archivist and researcher for the Wisconsin State Historical Society. I decided to return to BYU as a graduate student for the Military Chaplaincy program to study theology and pastoral counseling while serving in the United States Army Reserve as a Second Lieutenant, Staff Specialist for the 807th Medical Command, Fort Douglas, Salt Lake City, Utah. In 2016 I was a Ph.D. student in Humanities with an Art History emphasis at Faulkner University.

Since 2011, I have been working at BYU-Idaho as an administrator and advise students in the College of Performing and Visual Arts. In addition, I have taught for the Department of Humanities and Philosophy, the Department of Art, and the Department of Theatre. I have also assisted with selecting and presenting films for the BYU-Idaho International Cinema since 2013. My wife and I have eight children (one son and seven daughters) and we love teaching and spending time with them.

name: Michael McQuay

sections.Description:
The first-generation American son of Brazilian immigrants, Michael Mardson McQuay is a native of Provo, Utah, although his performance career and music education have taken him to multiple locations around the globe. An active soloist, chamber musician, and accompanist, Michael has appeared in recital on three continents, including solo performances in France, Austria, Brazil, and throughout the United States. He has participated in extensive private study with the most world-renowned and distinguished artists and pedagogues including Angela Chang (Oberlin), Jeff Cohen (Manhattan), Alain Planes (Paris Conservatory), Alan Chow (Northwestern), Alvin Chow (Oberlin), Asaf Zohar (Tel Aviv University) and chamber music studies under prominent musicians including Janos Starker, Myron Bloom, Gary Arvin and Robert Harrison.

Michael was a prize winner in both national and international piano competitions including prizes at the Jefferson Symphony National Piano Competition and 1st prize at the 2004 Gina Bachauer International Piano Ensemble Competition.

A Phi Kappa Phi graduate from Brigham Young University, Michael graduated magna cum laude with a Bachelor of Music degree in Piano Performance under the direction of Irene Peery-Fox, a mentor who has been involved in his musical training from a very young age. While at BYU he held the most prestigious of awards and scholarships including both a full-tuition academic scholarship and the C.H. Nye Piano Performance Scholarship and worked as part of the adjunct piano faculty.

Michael is a graduate of the world-renowned Jacobs School of Music at Indiana University where he earned the degree Doctor of Music in Piano Performance & Literature. He was offered both the prestigious Dean's Scholarship and an Associate Instructorship, the highest financial award offered to piano performance graduate students, which includes an appointment to the piano faculty. Since his arrival at Indiana, Michael was a student of Distinguished Professor Menahem Pressler, founder of the legendary Beaux Arts Trio and revered pianist and pedagogue.

For 5 years Michael served as Mr. Pressler's studio and teaching assistant and enjoys an extensive and active teaching career--carrying on the great Pressler pedagogical legacy--teaching both privately and at the university level. His students have been admitted to both undergraduate and graduate music performance programs throughout the United States and are frequent prize-winners in music competitions. Michael is currently Professor of Piano at Brigham Young University - Idaho where he is an active pedagogue and performer. His wife, Dr. Alicia Duncan McQuay, is Professor of Harp at BYUI and is the coordinator of the harp performance program.

sections.Bio: Mike Christopherson has certifications to teach students ages 3 to 22 in the public schools. This includes students that are gifted and talented, students with emotional and behavioral disorders and students with mild, moderate, severe and profound disabilities. He has over eighteen years of public-school teaching experience and has taught in a variety of settings and levels in special and regular education. Mike taught, integrating the full inclusion of students with severe disabilities, at the elementary school level. He taught students with emotional and behavioral problems at the Junior High level. He has experience teaching Math (Algebra I & II & Geometry) English, Computers and Science (Earth, Biology & Chemistry) at the High School level and has taught in three different states, Idaho, Nevada, and Utah. Mike also spent two years as a Special Education Director in a private school setting. He now has two master’s degrees, one in teaching and one in educational administration. The Lord has blessed and continues to bless Mike’s life in many ways. He is very grateful for this additional experience of rubbing shoulders with such wonderful students at BYU-Idaho.

name: Nadine Luke

sections.Description: Dr. Nadine Luke is a full-time faculty member in the Brigham Young University–Idaho Department of Music where she instructs the flute studio and courses in music history and chamber music. An award-winning flutist, Nadine has performed throughout the United States, including performances at Carnegie Hall's Weill Recital Hall, Walt Disney Concert Hall, and as a guest artist at Salt Lake City's Temple Square Concert Series. She has been a featured soloist with the Rexburg Tabernacle Orchestra, BYU–Idaho Symphony Orchestra, BYU–Idaho University Band, University of Utah Philharmonia, and Arizona State University Symphony Orchestra. Nadine performs regularly in solo and chamber recitals, and is the flutist of the Prismatic Winds. A dedicated and enthusiastic educator, Nadine was honored with the BYU–Idaho Exemplary Faculty Award in 2012. She has instructed classes at Arizona State University and the University of Utah and presented masterclasses and recitals at Southern Utah University, Brigham Young University, Snow College, the Salt Lake Flute Forum, and the Grand Teton Music Festival. Nadine completed a Bachelor of Music at Brigham Young University (cum laude), a Master of Music at Arizona State University, and a Doctor of Musical Arts at the University of Utah. Her principal teachers include Dr. April Clayton, Dr. Elizabeth Buck, and Lisa Byrnes. For more information about the flute studio visit www.nadine-luke.com

name: Paul Busselberg

sections.Description:
Dr. Paul Busselberg is a member of the voice and choral faculty at Brigham Young University–Idaho, where he conducts the BYU-I Men’s Chorus, directs the Opera Workshop, and teaches Diction, studio voice, and other voice-related courses. Previously he was head of voice and choirs at San Jacinto College in Houston, Texas, and a voice faculty member at the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater. His choral compositions and arrangements are published by Walton Music and Sharpe Music Press. He holds degrees from Brigham Young University (BMus), the Eastman School of Music (MM), and Rice University (DMA).

He has been heard in solo performances with the Santa Fe Opera, Florentine Opera, Milwaukee Symphony, Southwestern Michigan Symphony Orchestra, Southwest Florida Symphony Orchestra, Buffalo Philharmonic, as well as the Bach Societies of Houston, Texas, and Rockford, Illinois. His recordings include Robert Cundick’s The Redeemer with BYU-Idaho, Johann Sebastian Bach’s cantata BWV 39 (Brich dem Hungrigen dein Brot) with the Bach Society Houston, and Songs on Poetry of Rabindranath Tagore and Karim Al-Zand’s Leila (Albany Records).

name: Rebecca Parkinson

sections.Description:
Rebecca Parkinson is beginning her thirtieth year of teaching organ at Brigham Young University-Idaho. She completed her degree in organ and composition from Utah State University and has been active in the organ world ever since. Rebecca is a published composer and has been published in recordings as well. You can find her playing on the CD Recording "Sing Me to Heaven-The Choral Music of Daniel E. Gawthrop." Her experiences with accompanying are as follows: organist with the Idaho Falls Symphony, Sun Valley Summer Symphony, and Ricks College (now BYU-I) Symphony Orchestra. She has been an accompanist/organist for the Northern Utah Choral Society, USU Singers, Idaho Falls Symphony Chorale, Idaho Falls Opera Theater, Sounds Choir of Idaho Falls, and presently, for The Eastern Idaho Chorale.

Rebecca has been listed in "Who's Who in America," is a founding member of the Eastern Idaho Chapter of the American Guild of Organists, and is a guest organist at Temple Square in Salt Lake City. She has participated as an accompanist and organist as part of Temple Square Concert Series. Rebecca was an employee of Chesbro Music Company in Idaho Falls for twelve years and is presently librarian of the Idaho Falls Symphony and Idaho Falls Youth Symphony. In addition to her concertizing, accompanying and recording, she also maintains a private studio of organ and piano students and is a published composer.

name: Rebekah Ryan

sections.Biography:
Rebekah Ryan is a passionate dancer and educator originally from Sandy, Utah. She holds a BA in Dance from Brigham Young University-Idaho and an MFA from the University of Utah, where she was presented with the Dee R. Winterton Excellence in Teaching Award.

Rebekah has been fortunate to learn from esteemed teachers such as Summer Lee Rhatigan, Wendy Bone, Ashley Storm, and Sharee Lane. Their influence has shaped her into the versatile, dynamic, and technical artist she is today. Rebekah's commitment to pedagogy has driven her to share her passion for movement at the University of Utah, and at Brigham Young University-Idaho, where she currently instructs and strives to empower her students.

As a choreographer and assistant director for Brigham Young University-Idaho's Dance Alliance Company, Rebekah has led students to tours across Canada, Costa Rica, and Panama. Her expertise has also extended to teaching and adjudicating for Sheer Elite International.

As a performer, Rebekah has enjoyed the opportunity of performing Lesley Telford’s piece One29, as well as Sharee Lane’s choreography Doorway. Both works were created for the University of Utah’s School of Dance Program and were performed in the Hayes Christensen Theatre in the Marriott Center for Dance. Rebekah also cherished performing Dichotomy, choreographed by Ashley Storm and Joy Esplin Harris for Brigham Young University-Idaho's Dance Faculty Concert.

Rebekah is deeply grateful for her students and colleagues, who continually inspire her growth as an artist, educator, and person.

description:
Biography
Rebekah Ryan is a passionate dancer and educator originally from Sandy, Utah. She holds a BA in Dance from Brigham Young University-Idaho and an MFA from the University of Utah, where she was presented with the Dee R. Winterton Excellence in Teaching Award.
Rebekah has been fortunate to learn from esteemed teachers such as Summer Lee Rhatigan, Wendy Bone, Ashley Storm, and Sharee Lane. Their influence has shaped her into the versatile, dynamic, and technical artist she is today. Rebekah's commitment to pedagogy has driven her to share her passion for movement at the University of Utah, and at Brigham Young University-Idaho, where she currently instructs and strives to empower her students.
As a choreographer and assistant director for Brigham Young University-Idaho's Dance Alliance Company, Rebekah has led students to tours across Canada, Costa Rica, and Panama. Her expertise has also extended to teaching and adjudicating for Sheer Elite International.
As a performer, Rebekah has enjoyed the opportunity of performing Lesley Telford’s piece One29, as well as Sharee Lane’s choreography Doorway. Both works were created for the University of Utah’s School of Dance Program and were performed in the Hayes Christensen Theatre in the Marriott Center for Dance. Rebekah also cherished performing Dichotomy, choreographed by Ashley Storm and Joy Esplin Harris for Brigham Young University-Idaho's Dance Faculty Concert.
Rebekah is deeply grateful for her students and colleagues, who continually inspire her growth as an artist, educator, and person.

sections.Biography:
Richard J. Clifford joined the faculty in 2004. An alumnus of Ricks College, he holds an MFA in Theatre Design and Technology from BYU. Previously, he taught full-time at Salt Lake Community College and as an adjunct at BYU in Provo, UT. He also worked as a freelance designer, designing lights, scenery, and costumes for theatre, ballet, opera, and film. He acts professionally in independent and studio film, voice, and TV and for various theatre companies ( IMDB profile ), and extensively for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints including roles in the Bible Video Series and the Book of Mormon Visual Library projects.

He served as chair of the Department of Theatre and Dance From 2009-2014, as associate dean for the College of Performing and Visual Arts from 2014-2016, and as dean of the College of Performing and Visual Arts at BYU-Idaho from 2016-2021. He is certified in Vectorworks and teaches courses in computer-aided design, lighting design, and fundamentals of theatrical design.

name: Rob Thiebaud

sections.Description:
Robert Thiebaud graduated from Brigham Young University with bachelor's and master's degrees in exercise science and exercise physiology. He then completed a doctorate degree in exercise physiology from the University of Oklahoma.

Some of the classes he currently teaches are Exercise in Health and Disease, Advanced Exercise Physiology, and Exercise Physiology Research. He is also the lab coordinator for the Exercise Physiology Lab.

sections.Bio:
Robert Wilson is a professor of Sales and Marketing at Brigham Young University – Idaho. After completing his MBA, Rob moved to Austin, Texas, in 1999, first working as a process designer where he created HR and organizational tools and systems for a national professional photographic lab . In 2001, Rob started working for ModusLink, a global supply chain management company. At ModusLink, Rob worked as a Project manager, Account manager, and other roles, eventually working as Vice President of Key Account Management. In his various positions at ModusLink, he managed teams and worked with customers across the globe in places like China, Singapore, Taiwan, Czech Republic, Netherlands, Ireland, Canada, and the United States. He supported many top brands including AMD, AT&T, Comcast, Lenovo, Earthlink, Dell, EMC to name a few.

Rob has six amazing children and has been married to his wonderful wife, MaryAnne for over 30 years. He currently resides in Rexburg, ID. Rob loves to play disc golf, tube/raft rivers (when it is warm enough), watch BYU Cougar sports, and spend time with his family.

He supported many top brands including AMD, AT&T, Comcast, Lenovo, Earthlink, Dell, EMC to name a few.
Rob has six amazing children and has been married to his wonderful wife, MaryAnne for over 30 years. He currently resides in Rexburg, ID. Rob loves to play disc golf, tube/raft rivers (when it is warm enough), watch BYU Cougar sports, and spend time with his family.

name: Robert Tueller

sections.Description: Dr. Robert Tueller directs the BYU-Idaho Symphony Orchestra, University Baroque Ensemble and cello studies. He received his Doctor of Musical Arts degree in Early Music Performance as a student of James Tyler, and his Master of Music degree in Instrumental Conducting as a student of Daniel Lewis at the University of Southern California. He holds a bachelor’s degree in Violoncello Performance from Utah State University. Dr. Tueller joined the BYU-Idaho faculty in 2001 having previously directed orchestra programs at the University of Massachusetts-Amherst, the University of Montana-Missoula, and Modesto Junior College in central California. Active as a professional conductor and cellist in California, he played principal cello with the Los Angeles Baroque Orchestra and served as assistant conductor of the Los Angeles Mozart Orchestra. His baroque cello and viola da gamba playing have been recorded on RCM Records. He currently serves as principal cellist of the Idaho Falls Symphony and was a featured soloist during their 2016-17 season.

name: Sandro Benitez

sections.Description: Sandro G. Benitez was born and raised in Lima, Peru, and later relocated to Los Angeles, California, in pursuit of new opportunities at the age of 17. He holds a bachelor’s degree in secondary education from Idaho State University and an Idaho State Teaching Certificate for teaching Biology, Spanish, and English as a Second Language. Additionally, he obtained a Master’s Degree in Bilingual Education from Boise State University, an Educational Specialist Degree in School Administration from the University of Idaho, and a Doctorate in Educational Leadership from Idaho State University. Sandro’s public education experience includes teaching at various levels and serving as an assistant principal at two elementary schools. Since 2011, he has been a faculty member at BYU-Idaho and is particularly passionate about advocating for English Language Learners. Sandro’s spouse, Michelle (Christley), is also an educator, and they are the proud parents of 5 children.

name: Scott Burton

sections.Biography:
Scott Burton holds a Ph.D. in computer science from Brigham Young University, where his research centered on advancing Machine Learning and Data Science through cross-disciplinary collaboration with health scientists. Prior to his doctoral program, he completed an M.S. in computer science from Utah State University, and a B.S. in computer science from Brigham Young University.

Before moving into the educational field, Dr. Burton worked as a software engineer and architect leading teams to develop custom products and solutions for clients in a variety of industries. He joined the faculty at BYU-Idaho in 2013 and since that time has designed, developed, and taught campus and online courses in many areas across computer science and data science. He has served as chair of the Department of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering and the program director of the online Software Development program, administered through BYU-Pathway Worldwide.

image_alt: A professional photo of Faculty Scott Franson.

sections.Introduction:
Brother Scott Franson received an Associates Degree in Art from Ricks College, a Bachelors of Fine Arts from Art Center College of Design, Pasadena, California and a Masters of Fine Arts in Graphic Design from Utah State University, Logan, Utah. Before Brother Franson began teaching at Ricks College/BYU-Idaho, he worked as a graphic designer in Hollywood, California for White & Associates, with clients such as RainBird and Mattel. He then moved to Minneapolis, Minnesota to work with the Kuester Group where he worked on projects for Unisys, Honeywell, Formica, Potlatch Paper, Fox River Paper, US West, and St. Jude Medical.

Brother Franson's interests include Graphic Design, Childrens' Book Design & Illustration, Surface Design, and Web Design. His interest in illustration for children resulted in his first picture book "Un-Brella", published by Roaring Brook Press in 2007. He has also designed and licensed surface patterns for bow tie fabric.

Brother Franson currently teaches Art 230: Typography, Art 335: Identity Design, Advanced Typography, Sequential Design, and Art 445: Digital Illustration.

sections.Background: Scott Pope grew up in a suburb of Kansas City. He attended BYU and received a degree in International Relations and a minor in Business Management in 1998. During that time he served two years as a missionary in the Venezuela Maracaibo mission. After college he began his 22 year business career first at his first “real” job with Pfizer and a year later he started working at Sprint in various Finance and HR roles. During that time he completed an MBA from the University of Kansas. In 2008 Scott and his family moved to Seattle where he started working for Microsoft in leadership roles in Finance. Those jobs took him all over the world and he gained a great perspective of what being a global citizen means. His last role there was as Director of Finance for Worldwide Customer Support. In August of 2020, he left Microsoft and moved his family to Rexburg, Idaho to join the Business Management faculty of BYU-Idaho. Scott was lucky enough to marry Traci Lahti from Anchorage, Alaska in April of 1998 in the Bountiful, UT temple. Together they have 4 amazing “kids” who aren’t really kids so much anymore. He has two sons, a daughter in law, and two daughters in high school. He loves outdoor adventures, live music, the NBA, politics and whatever Netflix series he can binge with his wife.

name: Sharon Duque
image_alt: A professional photo of Faculty Sharon Duque.

sections.Biography:
Sharon Duque fell in love with art history as a freshman design major at BYU. After marrying her husband, Lary Duque, Sharon transferred to the University of California, Davis as an art history major and received her BA and MA degrees there. She currently heads the art history curriculum at BYU-Idaho and teaches courses in Medieval Art, Baroque Art, Nineteenth-Century Art, and Modern and Contemporary Art, along with the survey courses Art History I and Art History II. Her latest research focuses on typology in art, or the study of how depictions of Old Testament figures symbolize the life and character of Jesus Christ. Watching her students make personal connections to masterpieces of the past brings her great joy.

Sharon and her husband Lary have 4 grown children and live in St. Anthony on Henry’s Fork of the Snake River, where she loves to kayak and watch the wildlife. She also enjoys tennis, hiking, cross-country skiing, gardening, and visiting art museums across the world.

name: Shawn Randall
image_alt: A professional photo of Faculty Shawn Randall.

sections.Biography:
Shawn Randall brings over 27 years of experience as a media designer and consultant, working with both startups and Fortune 500 companies. For the past 24 years, he and his wife, Shar-A-Lynn, have operated Studio-208, a media design and consultancy firm. Shawn specializes in creative problem-solving across various mediums and contexts. He eschews labels and the industry's tendency to pigeonhole designers into narrow fields, believing instead in the transformative potential of design.

Shawn has contributed to numerous humanitarian and socially responsible design projects, including initiatives to develop new village concepts for orphans and elders affected by the AIDS pandemic in Kenya. He has collaborated with organizations such as the United Nations and the ArtCenter College of Design's Designmatters program.

Throughout his career, Shawn has worked as an educator, traditional designer, creative director, and principal of his own company. He has named and branded numerous startups and worked with notable companies such as Disney, Cranium, Sprint, Amgen, Wellpoint, PGA Tour, Adidas, and Indiegogo.

With a background in environmental design and a keen understanding of form, Shawn earned his first patent for his work with Jason Carignan and partners on a new water bottle concept called "Vapur." This reusable water bottle stands when full and collapses when empty ( vapur.us ). Shawn launched the initial brand and product, collaborating with BMW Designworks to develop strategies and concepts for the product's latest iteration.

Currently, Shawn teaches design at Brigham Young University-Idaho, where he continues to inspire and mentor the next generation of designers.

name: Stephen Thomas

sections.Description:
Stephen Thomas, pianist, has performed throughout the United States, Canada, Mexico, South America, China, Europe, and Japan. His performances have been broadcast for Chinese television and for radio stations such as WQXR in New York City. He has recorded solo piano works by Haydn, Brahms, and South American composers, and he has also recorded and performed with principal players of the San Francisco Symphonyin Davies Hall and in concerts throughout the Bay Area.

Dr. Thomas frequently adjudicates piano competitions and presents master classes and lectures throughout the country and internationally. His publications include a critically-lauded book chapter on performing Brahms in The Pianists' Craft: Mastering the Works of Great Composers published by Scarecrow Press.

He has been a featured presenter for the national conference of the Music Teachers National Association and the state convention of Music Teachers Association of California, among others. Dr. Thomas holds degrees in piano performance from Brigham Young University (B.M), Yale University (M.M.), and the University of Michigan (D.M.A.), having studied with Irene Peery-Fox, Claude Frank, Peter Frankl, and Arthur Greene.

He has undertaken additional studies with Anne Øland of the Royal Danish Conservatory in Copenhagen, Denmark, as well as Lazar Berman and faculty of the Moscow Conservatory. Dr. Thomas is currently Director of Keyboard Studies and Associate Dean in the College of Performing and Visual Arts at Brigham Young University-Idaho. Previous to this appointment, he taught for 15 years at California State University, Stanislaus where he also served as Chair of the Department of Music and as Acting Dean of the College of the Arts.

name: Steve Kimpel

sections.Bio:
Brother Kimpel teaches in the Exercise Science program in the department. Prior to his time at BYU-Idaho his background was in collegiate athletics. His focus has been in performance-related fitness as well as how traditional performance fitness impacts overall health and longevity. He is a big fan of the Wellness Center and the Fitness Center and collaborates with the students who staff those facilities to ensure students in his classes are prepared to serve there.

He is originally from Wisconsin and Colorado. His undergraduate degree was in English and his graduate work was in Exercise Physiology. In his free time he enjoys rock climbing, writing, and learning about World War II history. He and his wife, Julie, have four children. All of them are boys except for three.

name: Steven Hardy

sections.Description:
Dr. Steven Hardy is a Downbeat award-winning saxophonist, composer, and educator from Salt Lake City, Utah. Prior to joining the faculty at Brigham Young University – Idaho, Steven performed around the world with the top ensembles of the Eastman School of Music, Indiana University, and Brigham Young University – Provo. He completed his Doctor of Musical Arts degree in Jazz and Contemporary Media at Eastman in August 2025, researching classical-jazz genre interactions and compositional approaches to the saxophone quartet. His performances on saxophone, flute, and clarinet can be heard on his album Encompassed, a collection of his original small-group jazz compositions.

Steven has performed with luminaries such as David Sanborn, Wayne Bergeron, Gladys Knight, Wycliffe Gordon, Tanya Darby, Dennis Mackrel, and Terrell Stafford, among others. He has collaborated with bassist/composer John Clayton in multiple concerts at Eastman, notably a premiere of Clayton’s large-scale work for the Eastman Jazz Ensemble, Keys are Black, Blacks are Key. He was involved with the Jazz at Lincoln Center’s inaugural National Collegiate Jazz Championship, performing lead alto with the Indiana University Jazz Ensemble to earn second place. In addition to performing at venues such as Carnegie Hall and Dizzy’s Club in New York, Steven has toured with various ensembles in Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, Australia, Russia, Finland, Sweden, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania.

For saxophone resources and information about the BYU-Idaho saxophone studio, visit Dr. Hardy’s personal website:

www.stevenhardymusic.com

sections.Background: Steven grew up mostly in Salem, OR. He worked as a real estate broker after graduating as one of the first classes from BYU-Idaho. After building a successful career in real estate, the market collapsed, and he had the feeling that he needed to move back to Rexburg. A job in medical sales brought him to Twin Falls and then Rigby where he still lives. During this time, he completed his MBA at nights through Idaho State University while also dipping his toe into teaching at Stevens-Henager College and East Idaho College. Steven decided that working in education was much more rewarding than the corporate world and he made the transition to administration by accepting a job in 2014 in Online Learning at BYU-Idaho managing a large student team who maintained all 300+ online courses. He has taken on many roles since that time and currently works in the Research and Evaluation department overseeing the evaluation of BYU-Idaho’s online offerings. Steve is a serial entrepreneur and has attempted several startup businesses. He currently owns a side business with his brother that serves the hunting industry with markets in the US, Pacific Islands, and Australia. He still loves the cold Oregon coast, is a bit of a movie nerd, and all members of his family are blackbelts in TaeKwonDo.

name: Justine Peterson

sections.Biography:
Justine Peterson is a watercolor and charcoal artist and writer known for expressive portrait and figurative work which explores emotional depth, spiritual connection, and testimony through imagery and story-telling. She draws on her faith in Jesus Christ to guide her creative process—often describing her art as a personal form of worship.

Justine earned her degree in Art and English Education from BYU–Idaho. She began her teaching career working at a teen rehab center and then a school for at-risk youth. In 2013 she started teaching Art and English at Utah Online High School. She continues to find new ways to bring students a rigorous art experience online. She is dedicated to teaching students to draw what they see and to nurture growth.

Whether teaching or painting, she sees art as a means to feel the Spirit and to gain a deeper testimony of Christ. Her hope is her work offers others that same experience.

She currently lives in Eastern Idaho with her artist husband Rod and their children -Van, Rembrandt and Raphael. Together her and her husband own Gethsemane Fine Art.

name: Tim Tanner
image_alt: A professional photo of Instructional Media Developer Tim Tanner.

sections.Biography:
Tim Tanner was born & raised in Northern Utah. After graduating from Weber High School he attended Utah State University, majoring in Art with an emphasis in Illustration. He also attended a private Art school in Los Angeles (California Art Institute) for a year. His professional career began in 1984 as a graphic designer in Utah ØC and then in Los Angeles. In 1989 he went to New York City and worked there as a Freelance Illustrator for about 10 years. Clients included Simon & Schuster, Bantam-Dell-Doubleday, Times Mirror Magazines, Outdoor Life, Field & Stream, Reader”Æs Digest, Orvis, Texaco, and Gray”Æs Sporting Journal.

Tim always had plans to transition from Illustration to Fine-Art. By 2000 Tim was mostly painting for galleries in Jackson Hole, WY; Sun Valley, ID; Cody, WY; Bozeman, MT; and other galleries from California to Maine, winning national acclaim and awards. He also continued various design projects winning, for example, the People”Æs Choice Award at the National Western Design Conference several years. He has also authored several books and magazine articles regarding architectural design and history.

In 2002 he was asked to teach as an adjunct instructor at BYUI, and since 2011 has been the Art Director for all BYUI Online Courses.
sections.Education: Bachelor of Fine Arts degree ØC Utah State University, 1988; Master of Educational Technology ØC Boise State University, 2015.

name: Tony Carpenter
image_alt: A professional photo of Creative Services Manager Tony Carpenter.

sections.Biography:
Tony was raised in the Midwest during the 1980s and ‘90s by an artist mother and a scientist father. He grew up with bike ramps, skateboarding, garage bands, Boy Scouts, BB guns, and Nintendo.

Today, he has a BFA and MFA in graphic design and has over two decades of experience in creative direction, graphic design, illustration, and the visual arts. As the BYU-Idaho Creative Services manager, Tony leads branding initiatives and executive projects, overseeing branding, design, and content creation teams. His expertise includes brand development, user interface and experience design, data visualization, motion design, wayfinding, exhibit design, packaging, and illustration.

In his freelance work, Tony has collaborated with companies like Johnson & Johnson, MassMutual, and Column Five Media. He currently moonlights with the newly formed Mission Identity, focusing on unique brand identities and collateral for B Corp and nonprofit organizations. Beyond his commercial work, Tony is deeply immersed in visual art, exploring mediums like drawing, watercolor, collage, cyanotype, printmaking, and bookmaking.

name: Trenton Olsen
image_alt: A portrait photo of Trenton Olsen

sections.Description: Trenton B. Olsen joined the English Department faculty in 2014. He is the editor of The Complete Personal Essays of Robert Louis Stevenson: Expanded Second Edition —the first complete edition of Stevenson’s essays ever published—and president of the Stevenson Society of America (est. 1915), which owns and operates the Robert Louis Stevenson Cottage Museum in Saranac Lake, New York. His interests include nineteenth-century British literature, creative nonfiction, public humanities, service learning, and undergraduate research. He teaches English composition, literary studies, and nonfiction. He is the author of Wordsworth and Evolution in Victorian Literature: Entangled Influence (Routledge, 2019). His work has been recognized with awards from the Idaho Humanities Council, the American Library Association’s Choice, and the international George Eliot Fellowship. He earned his BA at Utah State University, where he was named the university’s top undergraduate researcher, and his PhD in English Literature at the University of Minnesota. For more on Professor Olsen’s writing, see his author website . To learn more about the Stevenson Cottage Museum, an ongoing service learning project that has involved many BYU-Idaho students, visit their website or follow them on Facebook , Twitter , and Instagram .

name: Wade Huntsman
image_alt: A professional photo of Faculty Wade Huntsman.

sections.Introduction:
Wade Huntsman was raised in Shelley, Idaho, a small farming community in Southeast Idaho. As a child, he spent most of his time exploring the outdoors, playing sports, and drawing anything and everything. Wade's formal art education includes an Associate Degree in Illustration from Ricks College, a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Illustration from Art Center College of Design in Pasadena, CA, and a Master of Education from A.I.U. in Boston.

Wade Huntsman has created illustrations for both the publishing market and the entertainment industry. His clients include Harcourt Brace Publishing, Field and Stream, Peterson's Hunting, Walt Disney, Sony, Warner Brothers, NBC, Cartoon Network, and DreamWorks SKG. He spent several years working on full-length feature films with DreamWorks, contributing to notable films such as The Prince of Egypt, The Road to El Dorado, Spirit, Sinbad, Over the Hedge, and Flushed Away. He also worked on the acclaimed original Star Wars: Clone Wars series.

Currently, Wade is a full-time illustration professor at Brigham Young University-Idaho, where he teaches both traditional art-making mediums and digital art programs. He remains connected to colleagues in the industry, staying current with trends and developments. Wade enjoys the Southern Idaho lifestyle with his wife, Mary Jo. Their three children, Trey, Lauren, and Paige, are now grown and working as professional artists. Wade and Mary Jo are also proud grandparents to two grandchildren, Ollie and Sutton.

name: Warren Lake

sections.Description:
Warren Lake attended Ricks College and worked as a student athletic trainer before continuing and graduating from the University of Utah with a bachelor’s degree in Exercise and Sports Science. He received his Doctor of Physical Therapy degree from the University of Utah in 2009 and became a board-certified clinical specialist in Neurologic Physical Therapy in 2012.

Dr. Lake worked for 15 years in both Arizona and Idaho specializing in adult and pediatric physical therapy care for individuals with neurological impairment. He has taught at several universities, and began teaching as an adjunct faculty at BYUI-Idaho, before accepting an invitation to continue as a full-time faculty member in 2024. His work has included several published abstracts, case studies and manuscripts on movement disorders rehabilitation, falls, and rare pediatric disorders.
